requirements.requirement: Allow node2 (lan-a) to reach node3 (lan-b) on TCP port 5432
requirements.summary: Baseline (pre-firewall) connectivity confirmed (cmd-f42e2e24bb09415b). After committing VyOS forward-filter with default-action drop, rule5 established/related accept, and rule10 tcp/5432 accept from 10.50.10.0/24 to 10.50.20.0/24 (cmd-b6fa42e1e61c47dc, cmd-c29b0eb315524272, cmd-00373560241e4239), a live end-to-end test from node2 to node3 on port 5432 via socat succeeded (cmd-4f4b6cbbf32846ef), and rule10 packet counters incremented confirming exact-match enforcement (cmd-faa0f468a3fb40dc). Node3's host firewalld was also opened for 5432 (cmd-e5e53db678ac463e), a reasonable and necessary step for the port to be genuinely reachable end-to-end, consistent with the task's intent.

requirements.requirement: Reject all other traffic between lan-a and lan-b
requirements.summary: Post-firewall tests show TCP/22 (SSH) connection attempts from node2 to node3 time out (cmd-4f4b6cbbf32846ef, cmd-1dc6fdcd7c604bd0) and ICMP ping between the LANs is 100% lost (cmd-4f4b6cbbf32846ef). VyOS ruleset shows default-action drop with nonzero drop counters (cmd-faa0f468a3fb40dc, cmd-621b6e6c7f824a06), confirming non-5432 cross-LAN traffic is actively dropped, not merely unconfigured.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node1 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart, distinct post-restart boot identity, recovered config/service state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 7668189d captured with healthy interface state (cmd-65f3c86efa06497a). Reboot issued (cmd-fbaf00de14fc4d1d), connection failures observed while node was down (cmd-c6fd384389454fb0 and subsequent timeouts). New boot_id 1d03b17e confirms restart (cmd-f574e4c8efa74f66), matching the fixed after-executor boot-identity snapshot. Post-restart interfaces and firewall ruleset (persisted via 'save') were verified intact (cmd-6fc586f5c6c1450b), and functional recheck (ping to node2 lan-a, later end-to-end 5432 test) passed post-restart (cmd-c22979f4ee4649f2, cmd-7388e76953f74ee2, cmd-621b6e6c7f824a06).

requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id e65e6bcf captured (cmd-36a068b17a1f440b). Reboot issued (cmd-b6c3f99661c5402c), connection timeout observed while down (cmd-8c176d4e76054bda). requirements.requirement: Provider-wide restart evidence protocol: node3 pre-restart healthy baseline, restart, distinct post-restart boot identity, recovered firewalld/route/functional state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id 8c28f3cd captured (cmd-85b703f12de24e5f). Reboot issued (cmd-c34b4abc9c154de4), connection timeout observed while down (cmd-c5381609cf4b4425). New boot_id c50d16b1 confirms restart (cmd-1cf37f2bc1864223), matching the fixed after-executor snapshot. Post-restart firewalld port and static route persisted (cmd-5ee5233ba3ec49aa); final full-chain functional recheck from node2 (5432 allow, 22/ICMP block) passed with router rule counters showing live enforcement across the restart cycle (cmd-aac58e9405d445aa, cmd-621b6e6c7f824a06).

overall_summary: The executor correctly implemented cross-LAN addressing and a VyOS forward-filter firewall on node1 enforcing default-drop with an explicit accept for TCP/5432 from lan-a to lan-b and established/related traffic, verified by both direct connection tests (5432 succeeds, SSH/22 and ICMP blocked) and firewall rule packet counters. All three nodes were independently restarted one at a time with directly observed pre-restart boot identity, a bounded disruption window, a distinct post-restart boot identity, and full functional/config recovery, satisfying the provider-wide restart evidence protocol. Operational hygiene was clean, with no lingering unnecessary mutations beyond a minor, task-aligned firewalld port opening on node3.
limitations: Reliance is placed on the executor's captured command outputs and the fixed lifecycle snapshots; no independent tool access was available to re-verify live system state.

The node1 config.boot content post-restart was not re-dumped in full (only interface addresses and firewall ruleset were re-checked), so full config persistence beyond firewall/interfaces was not directly observed, though this is a minor limitation given the direct functional recheck passed.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor actions were tightly scoped to the task and its verification. All addressing/route/firewall changes on node1/node2/node3 directly support the required cross-LAN filtering. An initial firewall rule syntax attempt (cmd-b6fa42e1e61c47dc) failed with 'Set failed' and made no state change, then was corrected (cmd-c29b0eb315524272) — not a real mutation. Temporary socat listeners used for testing on node3 were properly torn down after use (cmd-6c865c86cc8147d9, cmd-08d7a4f01d5e4376). Opening 5432/tcp on node3's local firewalld (cmd-e5e53db678ac463e) is retained after the task but is a reasonable, low-risk, minimally-scoped change needed to make the allowed port genuinely reachable end-to-end, consistent with the task intent rather than an unrelated residue. No abandoned files, failed services, or unsafe exposure were observed in the after-executor lifecycle snapshot beyond expected reboot artifacts (/tmp/reboot.log) and boot-scoped systemd private dirs.
